dedupe_keys.name: concretecarb labelled concrete carbonation surface images

description: ConcreteCARB contains 903 labelled photographs of fractured concrete surfaces after phenolphthalein testing. Researchers at Universidad Michoacana de San Nicolás de Hidalgo in Morelia prepared different mixtures, exposed specimens to natural atmospheric conditions for 180 days and photographed the split surfaces. The collection distinguishes 431 carbonated images and 472 images without carbonation presence. Mendeley version 2 lists JPG images and specimen-level CSV metadata free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is a laboratory campaign; calendar exposure dates were not established. The documented resolution is approximately twelve megapixels, and metadata link images to mixtures, additives and water-cement ratios. Staining-based labels and controlled preparation limit transfer to field inspections. Image counts do not establish the number of independent specimens. Modellers could test carbonation-detection assumptions or inform material-deterioration components in structural simulations. model-opensees is related to structural response, requiring separate deterioration parameters. No image or metadata row was downloaded, and no classifier or carbonation-depth model was trained.
